one_line_description.value: The Threads API lets developers create and publish posts, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, and access insights on Meta's Threads.
one_line_description.quote: Use the Threads API to create and publish posts, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, and access insights. The sections below link to reference material and step-by-step guides.

has_public_api.quote: Use the Threads API to create and publish posts, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, and access insights. The sections below link to reference material and step-by-step guides.

api_type.quote: The Threads API consists of the following endpoints. Refer to each endpoint's reference document for usage requirements.

api_breadth.value: Broad read-write API: publishing/reposting/deleting, media retrieval, reply management, user profiles/posts/mentions, location search, insights, oEmbed, and token debug (~9 endpoint groups).
api_breadth.quote: The Threads API consists of the following endpoints. Refer to each endpoint's reference document for usage requirements.

auth_methods.quote: The short-lived access token response from the `POST /oauth/access_token` endpoint now includes `token_type`, for consistency with the app access token and long-lived token endpoints.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: Note: This feature requires the `threads_share_to_instagram` permission.

access_model.quote: The Threads API launch post, dated June 18, 2024, says the API is open to all developers and lists publishing, fetching your own posts, reply management and insights.

access_notes.value: Self-serve path: create a Meta app in the App Dashboard and select the Threads use case. A third-party audit states the API is open to all developers; no paid plan, partner approval, or sales contact is documented in the evidence. Production permission/app-review steps and the separate Threads ads API are not described in this bundle.
access_notes.quote: How to create and customize a Meta app with the Threads API use case in the App Dashboard.

official_mcp_server.quote: We found no Meta page, developer blog post or GitHub repository from Meta that describes a Threads MCP server.

webhooks.quote: Support for publish webhooks has been added.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Changelog-driven changes and deprecations announced in the Threads changelog (e.g., Tenor API sunset by March 31, 2026). No explicit versioned path scheme is shown in the evidence; the API is reachable via graph.threads.com or graph.threads.net.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: Tenor API support will be sunsetted by March 31, 2026.

verdict_reason: Meta publishes official docs for a broad read-write Threads API covering publishing, replies, profiles, insights, webhooks, and oEmbed. Access is obtained by creating a Meta app and selecting the Threads use case, with OAuth-based tokens and no documented paid plan or sales contact. Missing operational details (rate-limit numbers, sandbox, official SDKs) are evidence gaps rather than documented gates. The only notable caution is that production permission/app-review requirements are not captured in this bundle.
open_questions: Do Threads API permissions require Meta app review or advanced access for production use? Not documented in the evidence bundle.
Rate-limit numbers: a third-party audit references a Threads API overview with rate limits, but the actual numbers were not captured.
Official Threads MCP server: a third-party audit (Oct 28, 2026) says Meta's only MCP server is for Ads at mcp.facebook.com/ads; confirm no Threads-specific official server has since launched.
Sandbox/test environment: a 'Threads tester user access token' is mentioned, but no documented sandbox is shown in the evidence.
Official SDKs: no vendor-maintained Threads SDK is evidenced; confirm whether Meta ships one.

Instagram account linkage: one third-party source says an Instagram Business account is needed, while the official changelog says Threads profiles without a linked Instagram account can now use the API; clarify current requirements.
Threads ads API: whether ads access is a separate API/gating track from the organic Threads API is not fully documented in the bundle.
Access model classification relies partly on a third-party description of post-launch open access; the official pricing/get-started page text was not fully captured.
